name: list_calendars
description: List all available calendars from the CalDAV server. Use this to get calendar URLs needed for other operations

name: list_events
description: List ALL events from a single calendar without filtering. WARNING: Returns all events which can be many thousands - use calendar_query instead for searching with filters (supports multi-calendar search).

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar to fetch events from. Use list_calendars first to get available URLs.

arguments.name: time_range_end
arguments.desc: Optional: End date in ISO 8601 format

arguments.name: time_range_start
arguments.desc: Optional: Start date in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z)

name: create_event
description: Create a new calendar event with title, date, time, optional description and location

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar to create the event in

arguments.name: end_date
arguments.desc: End, in the same form as start_date. For an all-day event the end is EXCLUSIVE: a single day on 2026-05-25 is start_date "2026-05-25" and end_date "2026-05-26".

arguments.name: start_date
arguments.desc: Start in ISO 8601 format. A datetime ("2026-05-25T10:00:00Z") makes a timed event; a bare date ("2026-05-25") makes an all-day event.

arguments.name: summary
arguments.desc: Event title/summary

arguments.name: all_day
arguments.desc: Optional. All-day is inferred from the date format, so this is only needed to state the intent explicitly; it must agree with the format of start_date/end_date.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Event description (optional)

arguments.name: location
arguments.desc: Event location (optional)

name: update_event
description: PREFERRED: Update event fields without iCal formatting. Use start_date/end_date/all_day to move an event or convert it between all-day and timed. Use fields for everything else: SUMMARY (title), DESCRIPTION (details), LOCATION (place), STATUS (TENTATIVE/CONFIRMED/CANCELLED), and any other RFC 5545 property including custom X-* properties (e.g., X-ZOOM-LINK, X-MEETING-ROOM).

arguments.name: event_etag
arguments.desc: The etag of the event (required for conflict detection)

arguments.name: event_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the event to update

arguments.name: all_day
arguments.desc: Optional. All-day is inferred from the date format, so this is only needed to state the intent explicitly; it must agree with the format of start_date/end_date. This is the supported way to convert an event between all-day and timed.

arguments.name: end_date
arguments.desc: New end, in the same form as start_date. For an all-day event the end is EXCLUSIVE: a single day on 2026-05-25 is start_date "2026-05-25" and end_date "2026-05-26".

arguments.name: fields
arguments.desc: Fields to update, keyed by bare UPPERCASE property name (e.g., SUMMARY, LOCATION, STATUS). Any RFC 5545 property or custom X-* property is supported, EXCEPT the dates: use start_date/end_date/all_day for DTSTART, DTEND and DURATION. Property parameters such as "VALUE=DATE" are not accepted here, and values must not contain line breaks.

arguments.name: start_date
arguments.desc: New start. A datetime ("2026-05-25T10:00:00Z") makes the event timed; a bare date ("2026-05-25") makes it all-day. Must be given together with end_date.

name: update_event_raw
description: ADVANCED: Update event with raw iCal data. Requires manual iCal formatting - use update_event instead for simple field updates (summary, description). Only use this if you have complete pre-formatted iCal data or need to update advanced iCal properties.

arguments.name: event_etag
arguments.desc: The etag of the event

arguments.name: event_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the event to update

arguments.name: updated_ical_data
arguments.desc: The complete updated iCal data

name: delete_event
description: Permanently delete a calendar event. WARNING: This action cannot be undone — the event is removed from the server immediately. Use only when the user explicitly requests deletion. Obtain the event URL and etag from list_events or calendar_query first. The etag ensures no conflicting changes occurred since the event was last retrieved.

arguments.name: event_etag
arguments.desc: ETag of the event for conflict detection. Obtain from the same response as the event URL. Ensures no changes were made since retrieval.

arguments.name: event_url
arguments.desc: Full URL of the event to delete. Obtain from list_events or calendar_query response.

name: calendar_query
description: ⭐ PREFERRED: Search and filter calendar events efficiently. Use instead of list_events to avoid loading thousands of entries. Omit calendar_url to search across ALL calendars automatically.

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: Optional: Specific calendar URL. Omit to search ALL calendars (recommended for "find events with X" queries). Only provide if user explicitly names a calendar. DO NOT use list_calendars first - that defeats cross-calendar search.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Maximum number of events to return (default 20, max 500). You get the earliest by start date, and the response states how many matched in total.

arguments.name: location_filter
arguments.desc: Search event locations containing this text. Example: "Berlin", "Office", "Zoom". Can be used alone as sufficient filter.

arguments.name: summary_filter
arguments.desc: Search event titles/summaries containing this text (case-insensitive). Example: "meeting with Elena" or "standup". Can be used alone as sufficient filter.

arguments.name: time_range_end
arguments.desc: End datetime (ISO 8601). If provided, time_range_start is REQUIRED. Both dates together form a complete filter. Do not omit if start is provided.

arguments.name: time_range_start
arguments.desc: Start datetime (ISO 8601, e.g., 2025-10-30T00:00:00Z). If provided, time_range_end is REQUIRED. Calculate dates for "today", "this week", etc. Can be used alone (with end date) as sufficient filter.

name: freebusy_query
description: Find free and busy time in a date range — use for "when am I free?", "am I available Tuesday afternoon?" or finding a slot for a new meeting. Searches all calendars unless one is given. Events marked TRANSPARENT (does not block time) and cancelled events are ignored; recurring events are expanded.

arguments.name: time_range_end
arguments.desc: End of the window to examine (ISO 8601). Required.

arguments.name: time_range_start
arguments.desc: Start of the window to examine (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-05-25T00:00:00Z). Required.

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: Optional: restrict to one calendar. Omit to consider every calendar, which is usually what "am I free" means.

arguments.name: include_event_details
arguments.desc: Optional: also list the events behind each busy block, with titles. Off by default — the answer to "when am I free" is the slots, not the meetings.

name: make_calendar
description: Create a new calendar collection on the CalDAV server with optional color, description, and component types. A timezone is accepted but not applied yet (the result says so). The URL is derived from display_name. If a calendar already exists at that URL, nothing is created and the error names the existing calendar — use it instead of creating another. If the URL is only held by something else (e.g. a deleted calendar in the trash bin), a numeric suffix is added (-2, -3, ...). Always use the URL returned in the response.

arguments.name: display_name
arguments.desc: Display name for the new calendar

arguments.name: color
arguments.desc: Optional: Calendar color in hex format (e.g., #FF5733)

arguments.name: components
arguments.desc: Optional: Supported component types. If omitted, nothing is sent and the server applies its own default. Use ["VEVENT"] for events only, ["VTODO"] for tasks only, ["VEVENT", "VTODO"] for both.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Optional: Calendar description

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.desc: Currently NOT applied: the calendar is created with the server's default timezone and the result says so (issue #78). Timezone ID (e.g., Europe/Berlin).

name: update_calendar
description: Update an existing calendar's properties (display name, description, color, timezone). Use this when user asks to "rename calendar", "change calendar color", or "update calendar properties"

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar to update (get from list_calendars)

arguments.name: color
arguments.desc: Optional: New calendar color in hex format (e.g., #FF5733)

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Optional: New description for the calendar

arguments.name: display_name
arguments.desc: Optional: New display name for the calendar

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.desc: Optional: New timezone ID (e.g., Europe/Berlin). Sent to the server as a bare timezone ID, not as the VTIMEZONE the CalDAV standard asks for, so a server may reject or ignore it (issue #78).

name: delete_calendar
description: Delete a calendar and all its events. WARNING: on servers without a trash bin this cannot be undone; servers with one (e.g. Nextcloud) keep the calendar in the trash for a while. Use this when user explicitly asks to "delete calendar" or "remove calendar"

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar to delete (get from list_calendars)

name: calendar_multi_get
description: Batch fetch multiple specific calendar events by their URLs. Use when you have exact event URLs and want to retrieve their details

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar

arguments.name: event_urls
arguments.desc: Array of event URLs to fetch

name: list_addressbooks
description: List all available address books from the CardDAV server. Use this to get address book URLs needed for other contact operations

name: list_contacts
description: List ALL contacts from an address book without filtering. WARNING: Returns all contacts which can be thousands - use addressbook_query instead when searching for specific contacts by name, email, or organization to save tokens

arguments.name: addressbook_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the address book to fetch contacts from

name: create_contact
description: Create a new contact (vCard) with name, email, phone, organization, and other details

arguments.name: addressbook_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the address book to create the contact in

arguments.name: full_name
arguments.desc: Full name of the contact

arguments.name: email
arguments.desc: Email address (optional)

arguments.name: family_name
arguments.desc: Family/last name

arguments.name: given_name
arguments.desc: Given/first name

arguments.name: note
arguments.desc: Additional notes (optional)

arguments.name: organization
arguments.desc: Organization/company (optional)

arguments.name: phone
arguments.desc: Phone number (optional)

name: update_contact
description: PREFERRED: Update contact fields without vCard formatting. Supports: FN (full name), N (structured name), EMAIL, TEL (phone), ORG (organization), TITLE (job title), NOTE, URL, ADR (address), BDAY (birthday), and any RFC 6350 vCard property including custom X-* properties.

arguments.name: vcard_etag
arguments.desc: The etag of the vCard (required for conflict detection)

arguments.name: vcard_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the vCard to update

arguments.name: fields
arguments.desc: Fields to update, keyed by bare UPPERCASE property name (e.g., FN, EMAIL, TEL). Any RFC 6350 vCard property or custom X-* property is supported. Property parameters such as "TEL;TYPE=CELL" are not accepted here, and values must not contain line breaks.

name: update_contact_raw
description: ADVANCED: Update contact with raw vCard data. Requires manual vCard formatting - use update_contact instead for simple field updates (name, email, phone). Only use this if you have complete pre-formatted vCard data or need to update advanced vCard properties.

arguments.name: updated_vcard_data
arguments.desc: The complete updated vCard data

arguments.name: vcard_etag
arguments.desc: The etag of the vCard

arguments.name: vcard_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the vCard to update

name: delete_contact
description: Permanently delete a contact (vCard) from the address book. WARNING: This action cannot be undone — the contact is removed from the server immediately. Use only when the user explicitly requests deletion. Obtain the vCard URL and etag from list_contacts or addressbook_query first. The etag ensures no conflicting changes occurred since the contact was last retrieved.

arguments.name: vcard_etag
arguments.desc: ETag of the vCard for conflict detection. Obtain from the same response as the vCard URL. Ensures no changes were made since retrieval.

arguments.name: vcard_url
arguments.desc: Full URL of the vCard to delete. Obtain from list_contacts or addressbook_query response.

name: addressbook_query
description: ⭐ PREFERRED: Search and filter contacts efficiently (name, email, organization). Use for "find contacts with...", "search for email...", "contacts at company..." queries. Use instead of list_contacts when ANY filter is specified. Omit addressbook_url to search across ALL addressbooks automatically.

arguments.name: addressbook_url
arguments.desc: Optional: Specific addressbook URL. Omit to search ALL addressbooks (recommended for "find contact X" queries). Only provide if user explicitly names an addressbook.

arguments.name: email_filter
arguments.desc: Search contact email addresses. Use for queries like "Gmail contacts" → "@gmail.com", "work emails" → "@company.com", or specific addresses. At least one filter (name, email, or org) is required.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Maximum number of contacts to return (default 20, max 500). You get them alphabetically by name, and the response states how many matched in total.

arguments.name: name_filter
arguments.desc: Search contact names (full/given/family name). Example: "John Smith" or "Smith". At least one filter (name, email, or org) is required.

arguments.name: organization_filter
arguments.desc: Search contact organizations/companies. Example: "Google" or "Acme Corp". At least one filter (name, email, or org) is required.

name: addressbook_multi_get
description: Batch fetch multiple specific contacts by their URLs. Use when you have exact contact URLs and want to retrieve their details

arguments.name: addressbook_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the address book

arguments.name: contact_urls
arguments.desc: Array of contact URLs to fetch

name: list_todos
description: List ALL todos/tasks from a calendar. WARNING: Returns all todos without filtering - use todo_query for searches with filters by status, summary, or due date.

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar containing todos

name: create_todo
description: Create a new todo/task in a calendar. Use this when user wants to add a task, todo item, or reminder with optional due date, priority, and status.

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the calendar to create the todo in

arguments.name: summary
arguments.desc: The title/summary of the todo (required)

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Optional detailed description

arguments.name: due_date
arguments.desc: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-12-31T23:59:59+02:00)

arguments.name: percent_complete
arguments.desc: Optional completion percentage (0-100)

arguments.name: priority
arguments.desc: Optional priority: 0=none, 1-3=high, 4-6=medium, 7-9=low

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: Optional status (default: NEEDS-ACTION)

name: update_todo
description: PREFERRED: Update todo fields without iCal formatting. Supports: SUMMARY (title), DESCRIPTION (details), STATUS (NEEDS-ACTION/IN-PROCESS/COMPLETED/CANCELLED), PRIORITY (0-9), DUE (due date), PERCENT-COMPLETE (0-100), and any RFC 5545 VTODO property including custom X-* properties.

arguments.name: todo_etag
arguments.desc: The etag of the todo (required for conflict detection)

arguments.name: todo_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the todo to update

arguments.name: fields
arguments.desc: Fields to update, keyed by bare UPPERCASE property name (e.g., SUMMARY, STATUS, PRIORITY). Any RFC 5545 VTODO property or custom X-* property is supported. Property parameters such as "DUE;VALUE=DATE" are not accepted here, and values must not contain line breaks.

name: update_todo_raw
description: ADVANCED: Update todo with raw VTODO iCal data. Requires manual iCal formatting - use update_todo instead for simple field updates (summary, description, status). Only use this if you have complete pre-formatted VTODO data or need to update advanced iCal properties.

arguments.name: todo_etag
arguments.desc: The current ETag of the todo (required for conflict detection)

arguments.name: todo_url
arguments.desc: The URL of the todo to update

arguments.name: updated_ical_data
arguments.desc: Complete updated VTODO iCalendar data

name: delete_todo
description: Permanently delete a todo/task from the calendar. WARNING: This action cannot be undone — the todo is removed from the server immediately. Use only when the user explicitly requests deletion. Obtain the todo URL and etag from list_todos or todo_query first. The etag ensures no conflicting changes occurred since the todo was last retrieved.

arguments.name: todo_etag
arguments.desc: ETag of the todo for conflict detection. Obtain from the same response as the todo URL. Ensures no changes were made since retrieval.

arguments.name: todo_url
arguments.desc: Full URL of the todo to delete. Obtain from list_todos or todo_query response.

name: todo_query
description: ⭐ PREFERRED: Search and filter todos efficiently. Use instead of list_todos to conserve tokens. Omit calendar_url to search across ALL calendars automatically.

arguments.name: calendar_url
arguments.desc: Optional: Specific calendar URL. Omit to search ALL calendars (recommended).

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Maximum number of todos to return (default 20, max 500). You get the earliest by due date, and the response states how many matched in total.

arguments.name: status_filter
arguments.desc: Filter by todo status. Use "NEEDS-ACTION" for pending tasks, "COMPLETED" for done tasks. Can be used alone as sufficient filter.

arguments.name: summary_filter
arguments.desc: Search todo summaries/titles containing this text (case-insensitive). Example: "write report" or "review PR". Can be used alone as sufficient filter.

arguments.name: time_range_end
arguments.desc: End datetime for due date filtering (ISO 8601). If provided, time_range_start is REQUIRED. Both dates together form a complete filter.

arguments.name: time_range_start
arguments.desc: Start datetime for due date filtering (ISO 8601). If provided, time_range_end is REQUIRED. Both dates together form a complete filter.

name: todo_multi_get
description: Batch fetch multiple specific todos by their URLs. More efficient than fetching one by one when you have exact todo URLs.

arguments.name: todo_urls
arguments.desc: Array of todo URLs to fetch
